claims.text: Rapid SPS will generate a refined grain-boundary network in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
Rapid SPS will generate a uniform grain-boundary network in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The proposed SPS schedule of approximately 1000°C, 50 MPa, and a five-minute hold is optimized for the target alloy.
Rapid SPS will suppress irradiation-induced Cr/V precipitation in W38Ta36Cr15V11 at approximately 8 dpa and 600°C.
The SPS-processed alloy will retain negligible irradiation hardening at approximately 8 dpa and 600°C.
SPS will improve the suitability of W38Ta36Cr15V11 for practical bulk fabrication.
Conventionally sintered nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 typically has heterogeneous grain boundaries.
Heterogeneous grain boundaries in the starting alloy act as nucleation sites for irradiation-induced precipitates.
The SPS-produced boundary network will have minimal impurity segregation.
A refined, uniform grain-boundary network will act as an efficient irradiation-defect sink.
Rapid SPS limits grain growth in the target alloy.
Rapid SPS prevents excessive grain-boundary segregation in the target alloy.
Reduced grain-boundary segregation decreases heterogeneous nucleation sites for irradiation-induced precipitates.
The controlled boundary network enhances point-defect absorption during irradiation.
Enhanced point-defect absorption limits the local supersaturation that drives precipitation.
The SPS-processed alloy will have at least an order-of-magnitude lower precipitate volume fraction than the conventionally sintered control.
Irradiated conventional W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits radiation-induced segregation or precipitation, especially Cr/V-rich phases.
The unmodified alloy has negligible irradiation hardening.
Approximately 8 dpa at 600°C represents the stated fusion-relevant applicability boundary.
